correctness.rationale: For each p=1,3, a spatial closed walk with its first site marked is exactly a p-row cyclic spacetime array; its initial row determines the rest. Thus traces count labelled configurations fixed by F^p, without a spatial quotient. Independent exact-integer reconstruction gives det(I-zA_1)=1-z-z^2+z^4 and det(I-zA_3)=1-z-z^2+z^4-3z^7+3z^8, with all remaining coefficients zero through dimensions 4 and 64. Another check lists the simple transfer cycles: for p=3 there is the all-zero loop and cycles of lengths 2, 3, 7, 7, 7 all through the pair (000,111). The three length-seven cycles are time rotations of the cyclic column word 000,111,011,001,001,011,111. In the determinant expansion the only disjoint products pair the zero loop with one of these nontrivial cycles, explaining the factor 1-z. Subtracting the fixed points from the third returns and dividing by three counts temporal orbits. The nonnegative log expansion gives support 7k+2a+3b with k>=1, so 7 and every n>=9 occur but 8 does not. The smallest positive Q-root r is simple and is its only root of modulus r by the triangle inequality and coprimality of 2 and 3; |z^2+z^3|<1 for |z|<=r excludes P-roots there. The logarithmic derivative thus gives the prefactor 1/3 in c_n~r^(-n)/3. The analogous P-root is farther away, giving the smaller fixed-state growth base.
residual_risks: Direct simulation is bounded at n=16; the all-size result uses the finite determinant identities and formal-series proof, not extrapolation. Neither basins nor other primitive periods are classified.

value.rationale: For a standard elementary rule already known to display mixed periodic bands, the shortest nontrivial temporal cycles provide a motivated exact recurrence test, independent of basin behavior. The evaluated determinant discloses three seven-column returns joined to two- and three-column returns at a common pair, explaining both the isolated size-eight hole and faster growth than the fixed-point count. This all-size structural law is useful beyond recomputing initial coefficients.
